Let's again presume that I'm indicted by a United States Federal Grand Jury for a crime and I'm in Vienna, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation through Interpol and the United States State Department through your Foreign Ministry ask you to arrest me. They follow whatever procedures are required by the Austrian-United States extradition treaty to get me arrested. At some point you are going to go --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But a legal person has to give me an assignment. It's not for me to be judging how -- what these international relations are. When I'm given an assignment, I carry it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Sure. Nobody's saying that, but at some point you're going to get paperwork from somebody that's going to say: "Go arrest Moran"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In this case it was the investigating magistrate.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: At that point you or some of the people working for you are going to go out, put handcuffs on me and drag me down the police station; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Now would it be the policy of your government or your police agency -- not your government but your police officers to question me about the offence for which I was charged in the United States even though it had absolutely nothing to do with Austria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the suspect is arrested, normally there is questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: And you would have enough information to ask me fairly detailed questions about the offence with which I was charged 10,000 miles away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Celebici, I think, is some 400 miles away.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Go to the next page on that package of documents. It's called "Search Warrant." Take a good look at it. I direct your attention to the last paragraph that says "Grounds"; okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Take your time, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: You are familiar with it? I'll bet you are. This is a warrant that authorises the search of several premises; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Six different premises, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: In fact, this is the search warrant you were talking about on direct examination, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is it of 15th March, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Now down at the bottom it talks about people being suspected of things; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: And there is a suspicion that there's evidence in these places; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever give, you or anyone acting for you or under you, ever give the investigating magistrate any facts to support these suspicions, or did you just say: "We think there might be evidence there"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are six different addresses which were believed to be in connection with Delalic and Mucic and we had done some prior investigation and we'd come up with these six addresses.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but did you give the investigating magistrate any facts by which he could determine that the evidence that you were seeking was there at these locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this is where the people were staying and that's why we thought it was quite logical that that's where the evidence would be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: But you had no facts to indicate that the evidence would be found there other than these people were staying there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The fact of the matter is that these people were accused of very serious crimes and that they were spending time at these addresses, and that's why the suspicion was that one might find evidence at those addresses.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: But you had no facts that there was evidence there, except the fact that these were addresses somehow connected with these two people; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but these addresses weren't connected just any old way with these people. There were some concrete relations. Taubergasse 15, Door 10, was the apartment of Mr. Mucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Judge, may I have just a second? Your Honour, I pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: We are almost always getting close to the time we should rise again a second time. I think we had better take advantage of that and rise so that when we come back at 2.30 we will continue with the cross-examination. (12.55 pm) (Luncheon Adjournment) 25 (2.30 pm)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Invite the witness. I see, Mr. Ackerman, you are standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. In as much as what we are apparently going to be doing for the balance of this week, and that is dealing with the Mucic statement, my client, Mr. Landzo, has asked me to ask leave of the court to not be here tomorrow. He would like to remain at the prison facility and work on what we believe will be next week's tasks, which will concern him. So he is willing, with the court's indulgence, to waive his appearance here tomorrow. I, of course, will be here representing his interests, but he would prefer to try to get some work done for preparation for next week. I don't know if there's any precedent for that request or not, but I can only make it and leave it up to the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But our rules say the trial has to be in the presence of the accused. Can we dispense with him?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I know we did that the other day when we were discussing -- not taking testimony and discussing matters. I think the accused can waive his appearance at least for a day where there is no evidence that has anything to do with his case. I think that's the case for the rest of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I think it is a right he can waive if counsel is there representing him. His mere presence can be waived. It is his personal right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You agree with this, don't you, Mr. Landzo? DEFENDANT LANDZO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: One totally unrelated thing. I have been told by the Registry that the witness has been using some documents I provided for him. Those documents have been marked. They have not been admitted into evidence but they are part of the record as Delic exhibits whatever the next numbers are, Judge. The Registrar made copies of them and included them just as documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Actually it was documents attached to an application.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Well, your Honour, there was one document that was not. It was the original German of a document, but all of those documents -- I think we used four documents. All of them have been photocopied by the Registry and are in those books over there at some place or other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What you mean is that the already existing documents are exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes. I have not moved to introduce them as evidence but they are part of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I did not think there was any need for introducing something. You were merely using them to elucidate certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: That was done by the Registry under their procedures. I just wanted the court to know that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: By your leave, your Honour, I would just like to draw the attention of the parties to the fact that the documents and exhibits, these are not exhibits. The documents that were presented to the witness and the copy of the translation in German that I'm putting in with the documents provided by Mr. Moran, they are simply numbered. It is otherwise an act of procedure in the courts. This is a document, not an exhibit. It is a document that does have a number. It is number D4/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: It does no harm to the presentation of the case. Carry on. It has no significance whatsoever. (Witness re-enters court) (Interpreter re-enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Moran, do you really want to tender the German original without the translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is absolutely immaterial to me. Whatever makes the Tribunal happy makes me happy. Whatever makes the staff of the Tribunal happy makes me happy. I think it was pretty clear from the record as it exists what occurred. I take no position on it at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms Residovic, you can carry on with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. Good afternoon, Mr. Gschwendt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic. I am defence counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic. Allow me to address to you a few questions having to do with your testimony today and regarding your role in the course of the activities in Vienna at the request of the International Tribunal. I hope you will answer my questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated before this Trial Chamber that you were a professional police officer; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My profession is police officer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated, Mr. Gschwendt, that you have some considerable training in the area of policing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, five years altogether.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated, Mr. Gschwendt, that lately in Austria you were involved in important activities to combat organised crime; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but just since a few days ago I changed departments.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will be more interested in what you were doing at the time of the arrest, or rather the search and confiscation of objects in the Celebici case. Allow me to ask you whether within the framework of your responsibilities you were faced on several occasions with similar operations of this kind, that is arrest, search and seizure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several cases of arrest and searches I have been involved, yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you always acted in accordance with the law on criminal procedure of the Republic of Austria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this case, too, you acted in accordance with the law on criminal procedure of Austria; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, Mr. Gschwendt, you had no knowledge of the rules of the International Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated in the Trial Chamber that upon the request of the Prosecutor of the International Tribunal you learned a day after the Prosecutor had requested the assistance of the Austrian authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me change the wording of this question; you know that the Prosecutor of the International Tribunal asked for the assistance of the Austrian authorities in this particular case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that this occurred on 13th March 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is when I saw the document in question for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, it is also correct, is it not, that you were involved in dealing with this case somewhat before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right as well, yes. The first request that was addressed, I believe it was received one week earlier, but it was just addressed against a Zdravko Mucic and only the year of birth was indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, are you aware that the International Tribunal requested certain information about Mr. Mucic and Mr. Delalic before this request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As best as I can remember, as said, one week prior to 13th approximately I heard about that and, as said, we really didn't know who this Mucic was. All we had was the name and the year of birth.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Gschwendt, that you stated in the courtroom today that you had obtained certain information on the residence of Mr. Mucic and Mr. Delalic to the investigating magistrate in Vienna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you collect that information before receiving the request for provisional measures from the International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know when that information was gathered specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, you briefed the investigating judge, Mr. Seda, of that information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I never talked to him directly. He received the papers from us.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on the basis of those papers, as you said, he issued warrants for the search of the apartment in which Mr. Delalic occasionally stayed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. On the base of our knowledge the search warrants were issued.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, a moment ago you looked at the warrant issued by the investigating magistrate in Vienna; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which relates to six addresses which needed to be searched?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, before the recess, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that warrant it is said that it was issued on March 14th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's two different times for these search warrants. The first search warrants were issued on 14th March. When we received them, we saw that they didn't cover everything and that's why a search warrant was issued covering all six addresses, and that search warrant was issued on 15th March.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for going back for a moment to the previous question. You said that you always acted in accordance with the law; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You are also aware that you are making this testimony under oath; that is correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm aware of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me if you received and learned of the request of the International Tribunal on 14th March and the warrant of the court is also dated 14th, when did you manage to gather information which you offered to Mr. Seda?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What you've said is not quite in line with the facts. What I said was that the initial information relating to Mucic was entered on the 6th and even then we began with gathering information about Mucic and where he might be found, and that the request from the International Tribunal came in on the 13th, not on the 14th. I have only referred to the 13th, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, I'm asking you specifically for Mr. Delalic. When did you first learn that it was necessary to gather information about Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also provide the information about Mr. Delalic to the investigating magistrate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the 13th on, these matters were no longer separate, because the cases of Mucic and Delalic were a single case, as it were, from that point on, and via the companies and via the club they were linked to one another.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell me whether you had information about Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did. For instance, we had the apartment here, the company, Taubergasse 14. The MAS company used to own that and we assumed that's where Zejnil Delalic would be found.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you were aware of these things on the 13th, when you received the request from the International Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that the Austrian police gave information about Mr. Delalic earlier on, much earlier than this, when you received the request for search and arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who's supposed to have provided that information.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, if you're not aware of that information and you don't know whether you knew anything about Zejnil Delalic on the 13th, which information then did you forward to the investigating magistrate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there was a bit of a mix-up there. On the 13th we did know, but the question was whether we knew before the 13th, and that question I cannot answer. On the 13th we received the request to take provisional measures against these two individuals, and on that basis then the arrest warrants were issued, but I thought you wanted to know if we knew something prior to the said date, and that question I couldn't answer.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore you allege that you received information about Mr. Delalic from the International Tribunal, and it was not you that had that information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the information, as far as I know, came from the International Tribunal via Interpol Vienna to us. On the 13th we had that information and then we received the search and arrest warrants.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, is it true that you knew on the basis of that information that Mr. Delalic occasionally stayed at the town Taubergasse 15 in the apartment belonging to the firm MAS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What date did you mention?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Taubergasse 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean the date. What date are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that date, on 13th when you received this information, were you aware that Mr. Zejnil Delalic occasionally stayed in the apartment in Taubergasse 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We knew that and on the 15th we received information from Munich that Delalic was alleged to be in Vienna.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know at the time that Mr. Delalic was regularly a resident in Munich?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 15th after we had been in touch with the German authorities, we did know that.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also know, Mr. Gschwendt, that at this address, Taubergasse 15, Mr. Delalic's sister was living together with her family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The sister of Mr. Delalic, do you -- the sister of Mr. Delalic, Ms. Hajna Delalic, is that whom you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is the sister-in-law. Did you know that she was living at that address?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we knew that she was living at that address.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Stevka Rizvanovic, his sister, did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We knew that and Ms. Rizvanovic was at the Koppstrasse. She was there at the search.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you know that several other families were living at that address?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which address?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Taubergasse number 15?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Taubergasse 15, there's three different objects at that address. There's Door 10, the apartment there, where Mr. Mucic was residing; Door 14, that apartment there, and it was assumed that Djemal Delalic may be staying there; and there's the ground floor. There's the Bosnian Club there as well as the company premises of the MAS company.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Gschwendt, that Mr. Delalic was a member of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Society, which had its premises at that address?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the ground floor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also knew that Mr. Delalic was a member of the Muslim Bosnian Cultural Circle, an association which was acting at that address?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We learned that he was to be there occasionally as well, but whether he was a member or not, I did not know specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, you also had information that Mr. Zejnil Delalic was never tried in Austria, never condemned in Austria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also knew that at that time there were no criminal proceedings being conducted against Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can also confirm, Mr. Gschwendt, that the Austrian authorities had no request or criminal complaint of other states against Mr. Zejnil Delalic at the time when you received the request from the International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say whether other police units may have had some other information. I can't say, but we didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, you collected all this information on 13th March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 13th-17th or 18th.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You provided all this information on 13th to Judge Seda?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And on the basis of that information Mr. Seda issued the arrest and search warrants for the apartment of Mr. Zejnil Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The investigating judge, Dr Seda, on the basis of our information issued the search and arrest warrants -- in fact, only the search warrants, because the arrest warrants were issued on the basis of the request from the International Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, you had no knowledge regarding the things contained in the apartment in which Mr. Zejnil Delalic stayed occasionally and in the business premises that he visited?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we didn't know anything about the contents of the said objects prior to the search.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, I understood you to have said this morning, and if I am wrong, please correct me, that throughout the operation you were in the police administration building, and that you were not on the spot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you designate the person to carry out the steps required by the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, once Mr. Mucic had been arrested teams were put together by me and they went ahead with the searches at the various addresses.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me who was in the team which carried out the search of the apartment in Taubergasse number 15, which was used by Mr. Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was Messrs Unger and Winkelmann.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: They are also police officers of the Austrian police, are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell me the team for INDA-BAU?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean at the address in Kopp Street?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was Captain Navarat, and two officers from the 16th District, Mr. Knauder and Mr. Klauser.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please tell me in addition to Mr. Unger and Mr. Winkelmann in Taubergasse were other persons present during the search, people that you had designated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Taubergasse there were two further objects. There were ten. Then there was the ground floor, the club and the MAS company and there were other officers in Taubergasse as well, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell me who was in the apartment used by Mr. Delalic in addition to Mr. Unger and Mr. Winkelmann? Was anyone else present appointed by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, what I can tell you on the basis of the papers is that in addition to those two officers the daughter of Mr. Mucic was present.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, you were the person who was in command of these officers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you cautioned these officers that they had to act in accordance with the law when carrying out the search?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Later on you received the notes on the search?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you did not later on check whether your police officers had carried out the search as required by law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, you'll have to explain that to me a bit more.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After receiving the report from your police officers, did you check whether the apartment or the business premises of INDA-BAU were carried out lawfully -- whether the search was carried out lawfully?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the basis for a lawful search was there, and as far as I could tell everything was fine.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you didn't check everything, did you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You'll have to explain that to me a bit more again, because when the men go out and carry out a search, and on the basis of the reports everything's gone ahead fine, then I do consider that I checked -- I had a look at those reports.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you. You didn't doubt that something unlawful could have occurred regarding the search or any unlawful seizure. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing could be done unlawfully, because there was a search warrant issued by the court, and at each of the addresses there was at least one concerned person or one person of their confidence present.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You confirmed a moment ago, sir, Mr. Gschwendt, that you were acting in accordance with the criminal procedural law of Austria; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in view of your training and practical experience you are familiar with the criminal code of Austria; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you always insist on the lawfulness of proceedings, because otherwise the operation that you carry out can be annulled by the court; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If a search is carried out unlawfully, without a warrant, for instance, then it can be ruled out as evidence. You couldn't use it. That's why there's no point doing something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and that is why you always cautioned the need for respecting the law; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The law has been respected.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You said that for the search of the apartment in Taubergasse number 15, the apartment in which Mr. Zejnil Delalic stayed, that you had a search warrant from the court. I have a copy of that warrant in German. Could it please be shown to the witness? (Handed to witness).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you look exactly at the search warrant, you will see that this is perfectly consistent with what I said. On 14th March there were four different addresses that were to be searched. On 15th March there's a search warrant where the six addresses are referred to, the six addresses I mentioned to you. Now this is the search warrant for the BIH Club. So this is one of the search warrants that was issued the previous day, but on 15th March there's a search warrant and in that search warrant you will find all six addresses. You should have that warrant as well.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have that warrant, but I gave up the warrant relating to Mr. Delalic's apartment at that same address. In addition to the joint warrant, the court also issued individual warrants for each of those searches; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not correct. This is a search warrant that was initially issued and precisely because there was information that was constantly being updated, on 15th March a search warrant was issued in respect of the six addresses I've mentioned to you.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We looked at that warrant before the break, and I am not requesting its correctness, but please look at this warrant as well as the warrant containing all the addresses. Will you please tell me, first, whether you gave that search warrant to Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not give that search warrant to Mr. Delalic, because he was not there. Mr. Delalic at that time was in Munich.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you convey that warrant to him in the next 24 hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I certainly didn't, but that wouldn't have been my job anyway. As you may know, Mr. Delalic was arrested in Munich at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the judge gave you the search warrant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I couldn't give it to Mr. Delalic, because he wasn't there. Not I personally; the officers who were there on the spot couldn't serve the warrant to Mr. Delalic in so far as he was not there.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never forwarded that warrant to him to this day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally certainly not, but that would not have been my job. As far as this search goes, Sanda Mucic was present, and two metres further on --

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, I'm not asking you about the persons present. I'm asking you about the handing over of the warrant. Does the court say in the warrant that this warrant has to be handed to the person who is being searched immediately or 24 hours later at the latest? Is that written in the warrant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. It's in the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this book, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's the Austrian law on legal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at it while I'm putting these questions to you, please? May I ask the usher to give this book to the witness? (Handed to witness). Will you please look at Article 140, paragraph 3, of your criminal code?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that paragraph? Does this paragraph also state that it is an obligation to serve the search warrant immediately or at the latest within 24 hours, without any exception; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's stipulated there.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nevertheless to this day you have not served that warrant on Mr. Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not present personally but, as is customary, as is always the case, the various people concerned or the witnesses were given this.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, are you also familiar with the provisions of Article 134 of the Code of Criminal Procedure -- 139?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 139 concerns --

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that paragraph 1 says that the search can be carried out if there is knowledge that there are things in the apartment which are of importance for certain criminal proceedings? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Is it correct that you stated in this courtroom that you did not know what kind of things were contained in Mr. Delalic's apartment and in the business premises of INDA-BAU?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the search you never know what you're going to find there. You are looking for certain things. If you knew beforehand what was there, then you wouldn't need to carry out a search.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, I'm not asking you about your practice. You said that you acted in accordance with the law. What I'm asking is whether this is stated in the Austrian law, and in the course of the request for issuing a warrant as well as during the search, as you said in this courtroom, you did not know whether in Mr. Delalic's apartment or in the premises of INDA-BAU there were things that would be important for this case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For Dr Seda, the investigating magistrate, there was evidence for incriminating Mr. Mucic and Mr. Delalic would be found here, and this suspicion was obviously so great that the search warrant was issued. The searches were not carried out without a warrant.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, is it true that Article 140 of the Austrian law says that the search can be carried out after previous questioning of the suspect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. If you look at Article 2, then you can see that after the questioning the persons concerned, that is here in this case the persons accused of war crimes, can be questioned -- sorry, need not be questioned.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There are only two conditions in that Article. If that apartment was empty, and this could apply to Mr. Delalic and not to Mr. Mucic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're not right. I'll read this article out: "With this questioning the person suspected ... if there can be a search carried out".

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not an expert in Austrian law, but I interpreted it differently from you now. So let us proceed, Mr. Gschwendt. At the time of the search, as you said, you knew that Mr. Delalic was in Munich and that he had been arrested; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your duty, Mr. Gschwendt, to act strictly in accordance with the court warrant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your duty to find in the apartment and seize only those things indicated in the court warrant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in the court warrant it was stated that you should find and seize those documents which refer to war crimes in Bosnia-Herzegovina and especially videotapes on the torture of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's correct it's stated in the search warrant.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you give the same instructions to your policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also correct. They had this search warrant with them.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, is it true that during the search of the apartment Sanda Mucic was present, a 16 year old girl?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Gschwendt, that according to the Code of Criminal Procedure it is clearly specified who needs to be present during the search of an apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not only Sanda Mucic was at this address, but, as far as I know, according to the information I had Ms. Delalic was also there, who also had the keys to this apartment. The door was not broken down, but Ms. Delalic provided the key here.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, I am not talking about entering the apartment but the search of the apartment and the seizure of things found inside. I'm asking you whether the persons found during the search and who participated in the seizure have to sign the report on the search of the apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The witness who is there must -- should provide a report of course, yes. That was not necessarily signed.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, will you tell me whether you sent with the two police officers somebody to make the report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The report is usually written up by the officer who is present at the time. It may be that apart from these two officers I think there were another number of officers who were also present and who worked on this case, and maybe some of these other officers was also present in this case. This is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you, so will you please answer: did you send with the police officers somebody who was supposed to draft the report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No. Did you send within the team for the search and for the seizure two court witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The officers have -- use witnesses who are available at the time on the scene. This was in Taubergasse. Mr. Mucic was there at the time, Sanda Mucic and Ms. Hajna Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, will you please look at the provisions of Article 142 of your code? Is it correct to say that a search has to be attended in the first place by the owner of the premises and of the things they contain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that if he is not there the search should be attended by an adult member of his family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Gschwendt, that if no adult members of the family are there, the search may be attended by a neighbour or a friend, who is also of age?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct in paragraph 3 of that Article it is stated that always a search has to be attended by two court witnesses and a record keeper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. One of the officers also is a record keeper at the same time. The record keeper is always one of the officers who carries out this house search.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And which of the policemen acts as two court witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You don't need to have two court witnesses, because in Taubergasse the following were present: Mucic, Sanda Mucic, who is only 16 and who is able to work but is not considered as a major and Ms. Delalic, Hajna Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is there any provision in the law of Austria which says that a search may be attended by a minor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not stated. You are right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the presence of a minor is against the law?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not contained or not stipulated -- what is not stipulated as being forbidden in the law is not out of the law.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So that is not in the Code of Criminal Procedure. That is not there. We must smile at that. Mr. Gschwendt, what you just told me about Ms. Hajna Delalic, you heard that from your police officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct and Ms. Hajna Delalic was the person who held the keys for this apartment, as far as I know, and is the person from whom these keys were obtained.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did your policemen tell you that? If they did, will you tell me which of those policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm afraid. I can't tell you any more.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the policemen tell you that they did not allow Hajna Delalic to enter the apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid I'm unable to say anything about this.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the policemen tell you that they pushed away from the door the sister of Mr. Delalic, Ms. Shevka Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are there any indications from the police concerning this?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you. Do you have any indications, because those were people living there, and they were not present at the search. Did they tell you that they did not allow Shevka Rizvanovic, the sister of Mr. Delalic, to enter the apartment that was being searched?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did your policemen also tell you that Ms. Raza Medovic, a major who was visiting one of the neighbouring apartments, offered to be a witness and this was not allowed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this, no.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, Mr. Gschwendt, to look at the reports of the search on the apartment in which Mr. Delalic stayed in INDA-BAU. I apologise for putting some notes of translation into Bosnian. Please ignore those words. Just read the report in German. Would the usher please give this text to the witness? (Handed to witness).

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May the Prosecution see also this document, please? MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I think we are entitled to that. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes. Yes. Of course. That's what I said, that the Prosecution could see the document. (Handed to Prosecution). Mr. Gschwendt, I can give you another copy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us look now at this report of the search on the apartment in Taubergasse 15 through 14. Is it correct that the names of the policemen are indicated as you had stated, of the policemen present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that as witnesses we have Mucic Sanda, who is a minor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only Mucic Sanda is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that we do not see any other name of a witness present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at the other report on INDA-BAU? Is it correct, Mr. Gschwendt, that in this report on the search of the premises where the names of those present should be indicated we have three numbers with four digits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I see the document? (Handed to witness). Yes, there are three service numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on neither of these reports is there any indication of a record keeper and two court witnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not correct what you've said. For example, if you are talking about the report with the three service numbers on it, there are two witnesses and there is not only this report, there is also a report on the search which was carried out, which should also be in your files. This is just what is conveyed on the scene at the time. For every search there is a written report, which tells you what time, from when to where exactly the search was carried out, and in this report there are most certainly signatures. This is not a record of the search itself. This is just the report on which the persons involved must sign in order to ensure that it was carried out, but this is not the report of the search as such.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, if I have understood you well, the second report is prepared by the policemen only when they return to the police station; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The report is drawn up at the police station. It's a nice typewritten sheet. It has the information about the search. Often this is filled out pretty basically, because this is filled out on the spot, but there must also be a report as far as this house search is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but this paper is left to the people present in the apartment; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The person concerned receives that. This is the paper listing the seized objects and that is why it's left with the person concerned or one of the witnesses, and the report is then drafted subsequently in the office.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and Sanda Mucic is not in the office when that report is being drafted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you agree with me then that in the report on the search of the apartment in Taubergasse number 15 in which Mr. Delalic occasionally stayed, you have as a witness only Mucic Sanda, a child of 16, and that the name of Hajna Delalic has not been entered into that report, nor of any other witness who could be a witness pursuant to the provisions of your criminal code. That can be an adult member of the family, a neighbour or a friend; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't have that report before me, so I can't really comment.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I showed it to you just now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once again, this is not the report of the search. This is a confirmation, as it were, as far as the seized objects go.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, as none of us are experts on Austrian procedural law, I just read to you a provision which says how a search is carried out and how seizures are made, and you agreed with me. So let me repeat again: it is carried out when there are suspicions that there are things in the apartment linked to a particular criminal offence. Furthermore, the search has to be in the presence of the owner, if possible. If not, then the search is attended by an adult member of his family. If that is not possible, then an adult neighbour or friend has to attend. I'm asking you: did any one of these people prescribed by law as having to be present when a lawful search and seizure is carried out go with you to your offices to draw up a third report together with the police officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean third report? The report that's drawn up at the office is the protocol referred to by law.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please show me this other report with reference to Taubergasse 15, the report that you drafted? Will you please show it to me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't have any papers along from the file.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you have come here to testify on the search and seizure that you were in charge of; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came here to testify, that's right, but I did not come here to introduce documents.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you carried out that search in your official capacity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that you have all the files. You probably have the search report as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interrupting. I would make clear for the record that -- ask the record to reflect that the entire file was previously made available to the defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: What is the meaning of that? She's asking for a particular report. Perhaps that report was not in that file. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): May I continue, your Honours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whenever there's a search, there's a report that's drawn up, and it's not a form we are talking about. We're talking about a typewritten report. It says "Regarding Search in Taubergasse 15 Report".

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify things. This report you are referring to now is drawn up by the team upon returning from the search and seizure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A member of the team, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And they do it -- and that member of the team does it in the police premises; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then witnesses prescribed by the law, the provisions of the law that we read out twice, are not present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They don't need to be present when the report is drafted. They need be present only at the search.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then they need not sign that report drafted by a member of the team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the only report that is in line with the law is the report with the signatures of the witnesses present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But it's not a report. It's not called a report. It's called "Niederschrift". It's a record. It's to indicate the reasons, for instance, why the search is taking place, and you have this also in your own language, who has ordered the search and which objects have been seized.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You have cleared up what this record means and who was present on the spot. Therefore, on the spot the persons envisaged by the law on criminal procedure of Austria were not present. Please, sir, can you tell me whether the people carrying out the search are duty bound to list the objects found and temporarily seized?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. You can see them there.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does that record have to be compiled in such a way that one can always clearly see what was seized in a particular apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For each address the objects seized are listed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told me a moment ago that it is your duty to seize the objects that are specifically indicated in the court warrant. The court warrant says that the objects need to be seized which relate to war crimes in Bosnia-Herzegovina and especially videotapes on the torture of witnesses. Will you tell me, please, whether your policemen informed you that they had found such material?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this concerned six locations and there were more than 100 videos that were seized, and they had to be viewed in the office first and analysed to see whether they were relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me please if you are unable to establish on the spot and immediately whether you have the objects indicated by the court warrant and you assume that they may be objects of interest regarding a criminal offence or a suspect, is there an obligation according to the Austrian law to draw up a special report of those objects?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Excuse me. I think we might break now for 30 minutes, because if you continue with this question, you will get into the recess we intend having. So we will come back at 4.30 and you will continue your cross-examination then. (4.00 pm) (Short break) (4.35 pm) (Witness re-enters court) (Interpreter re-enters court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Please remind the witness he is on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I should like to remind you that you are still testifying under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms Residovic, you can carry on. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. I would like to ask to facilitate things for us and the Trial Chamber let us clarify a few points. I wish to tell you that I'm questioning you because the Trial Chamber will be offered some of the objects as evidence found in the apartment in which Mr. Delalic stayed, and when I am asking you questions I wish to know whether the search was lawful, whether the things were confiscated according to the law, whether they were listed and whether that list reached the Prosecutor. Therefore, there are no traps here. I just wish to make things clear so that we can follow, and I would like to ask you to give me clear answers, if possible. I hope we understand one another.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also --

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: May I please object now to this general line of question -- to this continuing line of detailed questioning regarding Austrian law, because we have to know that the accused did not challenge the search either in Austria or under Rule 73, and the Chamber has indicated that if evidence was obtained in violation of international human rights an accused may nonetheless challenge its admission, but this, however, does not go into this. The defence lawyer is not talking here about international human rights. The defence lawyer is talking about minor formalities of Austrian law, which is not controlling in this case. So this line of questions on these formalities of Austrian law is not relevant in the submission of the prosecution. Furthermore, I would like to emphasise that this specific witness was called today in order to clarify the oppression issue, and this is the reason why probably Mr. Gschwendt didn't bring with himself all the file concerning the searches, for instance. So this is the reason why I object to this continuing line of questions on the Austrian law. We believe that Austrian law was complied with, but to go on on this line of questions would be, in our opinion, not relevant to this trial. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Turone. I wouldn't agree with you. I have been listening patiently to it and to the line of cross-examination, which is fairly clear. Counsel is trying to show the basis on which certain things were confiscated or were taken from those arrested at the time and in respect of the searches and whether there was anybody supporting the search and their detention of those properties, and I think whether in future it will be accepted or not is a different matter. Counsel is entitled to pursue the line of cross-examination. You can reply when you have the opportunity of doing so in your address, if you like, but counsel is entitled to seriously pursue that line of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Right, your Honour. Thank you. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honours. In the break I have been asked by the interpreters to speak more slowly and to wait for the answers, because the interpretation is going into several languages. So please answer my questions when you hear the full translation, and I will also wait to hear the interpretation before posing my next question. I have also noticed, since I have no command of German, there has been some imprecision in the translation of the document I've shown you. So please let us establish now that the record that is drawn up on the spot in the presence of the witnesses stipulated by law is the only record which is compiled on the spot, and which those witnesses have to sign. This record indicates the objects that were confiscating (sic) during the search. The exact name of that record in German is Niederschrift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Niederschrift, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it is the basis on which police workers later -- on the basis of this document police workers prepared the Bericht, the official report on the house search. Therefore I think we now understand one another. On the spot a Niederschrift or a record is drawn up, which is left to the witnesses, and in the apartment, and it is prescribed by law, and later your officers on the basis of that Niederschrift prepare a report. Have I interpreted correctly your words now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right. That's just what I said. This report is not based on the record because there's also further information. For instance, in the report it says, if necessary, where in an apartment, for example, at what specific spot a given object was seized. So the report is more specific, goes into more detail than the record, the Niederschrift.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we have cleared that up, will you please tell me whether it's correct that the Austrian law obliges the body carrying out the search, if things are not specified in the court warrant, to draw up a separate report on those objects? Will you please look at Article 144?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that those objects and that report has to be conveyed to the Public Prosecutor of Austria? He has to be informed about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you did not compile on the spot any separate minutes of things which are not relevant to war crimes in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the torture of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which objects are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's go back. You confirmed that in the court warrant it is stated that separate documents have to be gathered relating to war crimes in Bosnia-Herzegovina and videotapes on the torture of prisoners. That is the express instructions of the court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to the provision that we agreed on a moment ago, all other things needed to be listed separately in a report, and this report forwarded to the Public Prosecutor. My question is: did you make such a list of these other objects and did you forward that list to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apparently we seized only objects which were consistent with what is in the warrant. In the warrant it says documents about war crimes in Bosnia-Herzegovina and those are the kinds of objects we seized.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We'll come back to that again later. Tell me, please, is it correct that according to the Austrian law the provisions of Article 145, it is the obligation of the person carrying out the research (sic) to list with precision all the documents during the research (sic) and confiscating (sic) during the research (sic)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what happened. That was done. Now, if you look at the analysis, the analysis in respect of the whole case, each piece of paper was described, was analysed and described, and there are objects which were described as not being relevant, but you have to see what the police's possibilities are on the spot. It couldn't be done then and there. You can't have a look at 100 videos on the spot or if you seize a computer with a 3 gigabyte memory, what are you going to do on the spot with that?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, sir, will you tell me with precision your officers on the spot, did they take note of each videotape separately and each document separately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at the spot, not at the scene, but later on in the office the objects were reviewed and analysed. A video lasts 240 minutes. If you happen to have 80 of them, if you've received 80 videos, just imagine how long your search would last if you were to view them on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. Gschwendt, but is it correct that the Austrian law is familiar with such a situation when officers on the spot are unable to list all documents and view all videotapes, is it true that Article 145 of the Austrian law says that in that case all those documents have to be packed, sealed, signed by the persons present and kept until they are analysed under court supervision? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, but as far as I know there was an order from the investigating judge to analyse all of the objects.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, we are not talking about the court warrant. We are talking about the method of confiscating goods. The law says clearly everything should be listed in detail, and if that is not possible that objects and documents be sealed, taken to the police station or placed under court supervision; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that the investigating judge's order is sufficient and that that would not apply.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you -- please answer if you can, because you said that you were familiar with the Austrian law, and you have the law before you -- am I quoting correctly Article 145 of the Austrian law which regulates the way in which things should be confiscated, which cannot be listed on the spot? Have I correctly interpreted that provision of the Austrian Code of Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a question of time really. They were to be listed and they subsequently were listed. You would have to enter into a legal procedure about the definition of warrants --

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does not stipulate here, as far as I know, that it necessarily has to be at the scene of the search.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Please, counsel, is this matter not clearly one of practicality of what you are doing, because if, as the questioning has been going, you have a lot of things that cannot easily be determined on the spot, but they still have to be taken away. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Yes, your Honours. I'm just asking the witness whether they packed and sealed the things that they could not list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We listed all things -- so I said we listed everything, but it took a little bit of time. Each video cassette was given a number, each document was given a number, but 240 minutes times 80 --

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, did you in the apartment or in the premises of INDA-BAU pack or seal these documents in order to review them later when you have time? Did you seal the things that you could not list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the search we already began listing these items. Why should they have been sealed if you're already beginning to process them?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because that is what the Austrian law says. Please when listing these objects in the police station did you invite, as prescribed by Article 145, Mr. Delalic or his representative to be present upon the identification of the confiscated objects?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in this case it wasn't required, because they weren't sealed upon a court order, because he only has to be there if you seal them and then they are subsequently opened.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, will you look once again at the reports on the search which I gave you or showed you before the break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the record, the Niederschrift?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Niederschrift. Do you have a copy before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have this copy before me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Gschwendt, that in the record on the search of the apartment in Taubergasse 15, where the witness was, the minor, Mucic Sanda, stated 30 video tapes were found, various photographs, notes, documents, 2 berets, military trousers, military vest and a black sports bag; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, is it correct in the record on the search of the premises of INDA-BAU in Koppstrasse that it says that 51 videotapes were taken, newspapers, two registers connected to Mucic, two registers connected to Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you compiled the report later on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now with regard to the seized objects subsequently in the office a report was drafted and subsequently there was a second report that was drafted, and there's details there about each and every one of those videotapes, and they are each and every one of them described.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When confiscating these objects, did you place any signs on them which would guarantee that the objects that you later listed were objects that were actually found in the apartment or premises searched?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That isn't done at the scene of the search. Usually these things are put in a big box, and once you get to the office a sticker is put on them to identify them, and then they are processed. These objects are under our constant supervision. When there's nobody in the office, then you lock them up under file and key to see to it that nobody has access to them.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, they were given to the Austrian police in full confidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hope that people can have full confidence in the Austrian police.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, did you personally see those enormous boxes with the confiscated materials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did see the objects, but I didn't count them myself, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that in INDA-BAU thousands of various papers were confiscated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think thousands would be right, but there were a lot of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And most of those papers, about 95 per cent, were in the Bosnian or Serbo-Croatian language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't place any indication in INDA-BAU premises themselves so that you would know what the papers were -- where the papers were from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That should be in the report that we've referred to several times, but that should be in there.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Gschwendt, that some differences occurred between what was found in the records on the spot and what you later analysed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know there was one case I think with regard to the video cassettes. There'd been an error made in the counting by three and on that score a special report was drafted to set the record straight.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The report was compiled by the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please, Mr. Gschwendt, look at this report and compare it with the record made on the spot in INDA-BAU?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Again, may the Prosecution see the document? (Handed to Prosecution) (Handed to witness)?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's the report I referred to. There was this mistake made. Three units and here it's stated that there weren't 51 but rather 54 of them, and then there's a description there as to how they were identified. There was a mistake, yes. Somebody miscounted by three tapes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, will you tell me is it correct that in this record we find the figure of 51 videotapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought I told you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your report it says 54?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, and that mistake in the counting was set right. Somebody at the scene of the search miscounted by three. Nobody's perfect.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that that report on the counting was compiled on 22nd April?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If that's the date on there, if that's when they were analysed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the search was conducted on 19th March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 18th.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which three videotapes had not been counted during the search on the spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I certainly can't.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether from March 19th to April 22nd, 1996 a change may have occurred in the number of tapes which are not described in any other way except by their numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, listen, I've already said once, apparently a counting mistake had been made and it was set right.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The police corrected the number; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The police corrected that mistake. These items were processed by the police and that's how the mistake came out. It was discovered by the police. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Did you specifically indicate which three videotapes had not been counted on 19th March?

utterances.speaker: MR. TURONE
utterances.text: Objection, your Honour. Asked and answered already. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you. Can you, Mr. Gschwendt, look at the second report of yours, which refers to the search of the apartment in which Mr. Delalic stayed in Taubergasse number 15? A copy for the Prosecution too, please. (Handed to Prosecution) (Handed to witness). Mr. Gschwendt, this report was also compiled on 22nd April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What does "Niederschrift" mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Writing down.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Niederschrift" means record. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): On the spot. This report was also written by you in the police on 22nd April 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The date's on there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it stated in this report that in Mr. Delalic's apartment 28 videotapes were found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at the record made on the spot dated 19th March 1996. Is it stated in this record that 30 videotapes were found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this record there is no statement regarding the error. Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's right too, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Noting -- when the error was noted, the witnesses who were on the spot were not present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now the things we are comparing here aren't the same. The report here refers to Taubergasse 15, Door 14. No, no, it's right. There's a difference of two units, but it might also be due to the fact that there were some blank video cassettes, but I would rather not comment on that. I simply don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, is it correct that neither you nor the officers working under you can describe the tapes with precision, the tapes that were missing from Mr. Delalic's apartment, nor the tapes that appeared subsequently from the INDA-BAU premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of the videotapes were described individually and on the basis of that description one should be able to clear up that mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A mistake regarding the tapes that were not counted on the 19th March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there and I didn't count these things, so I'm the wrong person to put that question to.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Didn't you just tell me -- did you just confirm that nobody had put any markers on the things that were brought to the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I said was each individual item was identified, but -- each in turn. There were a lot of things there.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it may have occurred tomorrow, in a week, in a month, since there were a lot of objects; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see this on the basis of the dates on the reports.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me: is it correct that the objects taken from the premises of Mr. Delalic were served on the Hague Tribunal only after you had analysed those documents?
