utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some things were copied with the approval of the investigating magistrate and these were transmitted to members of the Tribunal. That is also contained in the report which things this concerned exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that if there is no report or copies sent to the International Tribunal, then the remaining objects were not transmitted before they were fully analysed and identified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This should be contained in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that on the basis of the documents that defence counsel has received there is a report that you photocopied the videotapes found with Mr. Zdravko Mucic and that they were transmitted to the Tribunal, is it then correct to say that the things you found with Mr. Delalic, about which there is no report on their transmission to the Tribunal, that they were, in fact, transmitted according to the report dated end of April 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These objects which were transmitted to the Tribunal, they were also described but I can't say exactly whether they concern Mucic or Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, if there is a report, then things are as is stated in the report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that should be the case.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, we have seen now what errors occurred with regard to the videotapes. You confirmed that in Mr. Delalic's apartment and in INDA-BAU a large quantity of material was found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was most of that material understandable to you when you received it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this question you're asking me, I am not the right person to ask. I was not the person who viewed and analysed all these things. I distributed the work on this.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Will you please tell me who is the right person to address and who can confirm this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see this on the analysis reports, the people who -- person who has written about a specific thing is the person who dealt with this, but I can't just tell you which officer was responsible for every individual video cassette, just off the cuff, but this is described and the person who made the report is the person who worked on these objects.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you told me a moment ago that you saw a large quantity of documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them indeed, but, I mean, I saw them but I didn't work on them myself.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And they, too, were not marked in any way when they were brought to the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are starting with the same problem every time. They were carried out according to capacity, dealt with according to the capacity we had.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask you to take a look at these documents and to see whether that belongs to that pile of material that you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You don't need to show them to me, because I can't recognise a document from 25 different binders, one single document. I did not carry out this analysis personally.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Particularly not if they were not marked. Will you tell me whether Mr. -- I'm sorry, the witness coming after you -- Moerbauer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Moerbauer, could he answer these questions? Is that so, and Mr. Panzer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Moerbauer will certainly be able to answer part of these questions, because he dealt with, processed part of this material.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with these objects I would like to ask for the following: when you served them on the International Tribunal the things that you allegedly confiscated in the apartment and the business premises in which Mr. Delalic stayed, did you make a receipt on the handing over of that material?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know these things were not given to the International Tribunal by us, but by the court. Upon the conclusion of this, all of the material, along with the analysis, was handed over to the court.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When serving this on the court or, rather, the International Tribunal, did you inform Mr. Delalic accordingly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was not my duty. If the items are with the court, they're outside the sphere of influence of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as I have understood you, you said that Mr. Moerbauer could confirm a part of those things. Will you tell me who can confirm the rest of these things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You'll have to look at the signatures of the officers who processed that.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And who can confirm the objects that are insignificant, as you said a moment ago, and which are not a part of your analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean? Which objects are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have read your reports. A part of the documents was processed. Others are said to be not interesting. I would like to know who can confirm that at Mr. Delalic's things were confiscated that were not analysed by anybody in their report and which were also transferred to the International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, those items that were significant in connection with the search warrant issued by the court, they were translated, viewed and then they were -- rather than translated shall we say interpreted, and these items are listed. For instance -- well, take a newspaper article that was not in any way connected to the case. It was not given any reference, because it served no purpose as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gschwendt, this part of the questioning relating to the confiscation of objects I think I have more or less rounded off, and since you have the Code on Criminal Procedure of Austria before you, would you agree with me if I say that during the search confiscation, listing, sealing, unsealing and transmission of objects your bodies acted contrary to the provisions of Articles 139, 140, 141, 142, 143, 144 and 145 of the Code on Criminal Procedure and outside the mandate issued by the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't agree with that at all. There were a few mistakes that were made. For instance, there was a miscount of three videotapes. There's an age difference of two years, but those are the only mistakes that were made and those are in there. They've been documented. Nobody would try to hide any of this. Mistakes happen.

utterances.speaker: MS RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Allow me to put to you a few questions about the topic you testified to this morning. You were shown a form -- I don't have very much?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Well, I really don't mind. If you still have anything to put to him, if you have any questions which are worth pursuing now, you can do this. Because it doesn't appear everyone is done with this witness, you may still continue tomorrow morning. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Except if you have no major things to ask tomorrow morning, but we can continue tomorrow morning. MS. RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Your Honours, I have a set of questions which will not take long. Whether I do that now or tomorrow morning, it will not take more than half an hour, maybe less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE
utterances.text: Half an hour is suitable for tomorrow morning. The Trial Chamber will rise now and continue tomorrow morning. (5.30 pm)
